text:
maya: quick debrief — ran a quick sanity quant run for zebra-34b KV-only (FP8 vs INT8) on a small 12-node pool. collecting notes here.
ajay: nice, what exactly did you quantize? whole model or KV only?
maya: KV-only (keys + values). left dense weights in fp16. reason: minimize accuracy drift while getting memory wins.
lina: what configs? can you paste the runtime flags you used?
maya: sure:
```
--model zebra-34b
--quant-mode kv-only
--kv-quant {type: fp8,scaling: per-tensor}
--fallback gptq-compat:off
--batch-size 4
--prefill-cache true
```
sasha: results? numbers speak 😅
maya: summary: FP8-KV -> ~26% GPU memory reduction on the per-shard KV buffers, p50 steady-state token latency ~+1.8ms (~3.2% increase), cold-start increase ~+18ms. INT8-KV -> ~40% memory reduction, p50 latency +4.6ms (~8.2%), cold-start +42ms.
kai: how about quality? any eval regressions on the smoke prompts?
maya: ran our regression set (300 prompts: QA + instruction-following + long-context summarization). FP8-KV: delta accuracy -0.4% (within noise), rouge-l drop 0.5 on long summaries. INT8-KV: delta accuracy -1.9%, rouge-l -1.8 on long-context; two failure cases where answer truncated mid-sentence more often.
ajay: did you try hybrid — fp8 for keys, int8 for values or vice-versa?
maya: yes: keys=fp8, vals=int8 gave memory ~36% reduction and latency +3.1ms, quality delta -1.1%. looks like values quantization hurts generation quality more.
lina: any insights into cold-start regression source? I assume dequant path adds overhead to KV warmup.
maya: exact trace shows extra memcpy + dequant on first access. Kernel scheduling causes small stalls. I pasted a short perf log:
```
[perf] prefill: init-kv 12.3ms -> dequant 15.9ms -> first-token 7.1ms
[perf] steady: attn-kv-access 0.45ms (fp16) vs 0.98ms (int8-dequant)
```
sasha: can we mitigate by async dequant on prefill or prewarming thread pool?
ajay: we can try async background dequant + prioritizing prefill RPC to do dequant before returning. risk: memory peak if we keep both copies.
kai: what's the plan for canary? I'm wary of INT8-KV due to the ~2% quality hit.
maya: proposal:
- FP8-KV: run a 24h canary on dedicated infra (10% traffic) with eval hooks and quality monitors.
- Hybrid (keys fp8, vals int8): smoke on 6h then decide.
- INT8-KV full: keep in experiments, but block wide rollout until we fix truncation pattern.
lina: for FP8-KV canary, add an automatic fallback to fp16 if model-level regression trigger >0.8% on our daily QA set.
ajay: ops note: FP8 kernel path currently uses our new fused-dequant kernel; need to lift OOM checks for certain shard sizes. I'll patch the scheduler.
deploy-bot: canary scheduled: zebra-34b-fp8-kv-canary -> start 2026-03-22T02:00Z -> 24h -> target 10% traffic
sasha: timeline + owners?
maya: owner for canary + eval: maya. ops owner: ajay. ML/analysis: lina. rollout decision checkpoint 2026-03-23 02:30Z UTC.
kai: small ask: add a short prompt-set targeting long-context QA where vals quant affects coherence. I have 20 edge cases.
maya: send them to me in thread and I'll add to canary scoring.
ajay: I'll prototype async dequant prefill branch this week and post perf diffs.
lina: also add a distribution of seq-lens to the canary so we can see if tail latency regresses for >4k tokens.
sasha: :thumbsup: good plan, thanks all.
maya: thanks — will open a short runbook + PR with flags and the canary ID after lunch.
kai: :eyes: looking forward to the runbook.
